newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei tops key 19,000 level on U.S. rally.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei tops key 19,000 level on U.S. rally.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index topped the 19,000 barrier on Wednesday morning, encouraged by a steep rise on Wall Street on Tuesday.
The Nikkei 225 index rose above the key level for the first time since February 28.
By 0118 GMT, the key 225-share Nikkei average had climbed 368.33 points or 1.97 percent to 19,038.70. June Nikkei futures had added 420 points to reach 19,070.
"The U.S. stock surge has erased one unclear factor that Tokyo was worried about," said Seiki Orimi, manager of stock information services at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
There had been fears in Tokyo that strong U.S. economic data might hit the Dow this week and that any sharp decline in U.S. stocks could damage Japanese stocks, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the Dow industrials closed up 179 points or 2.65 percent at 6,962.
